channel.title: Am I affected? changelog
channel.description: Every check added to Am I affected?, newest first.

item.title: Watch mode stays quiet when an update doesn't fix anything
item.description: A kernel or package update that leaves the same bug open is no longer reported as one new and one fixed finding. Found by running watch mode on our own server.

item.title: Kernel advice no longer mentions AlmaLinux on Ubuntu
item.description: A note meant for RHEL-family servers was shown on every distro.

item.title: Watch mode for servers
item.description: Run it daily from cron with --watch and hear only about new and fixed findings, by webhook (Slack, Teams, Discord) or through your own sendmail. A quiet day sends nothing.

item.title: GitHub Action
item.description: uses: abhay-avagama/security-inspector@v1 checks a repository on every push: pinned packages, MCP configs, agent skills and .env files, never the runner itself.

item.title: Skill change tracking
item.description: --skills-baseline FILE records a fingerprint of every installed agent skill and lists new skills and changed files on the next run.

item.title: Agent skill and hook audit
item.description: Every installed skill is checked for hidden instructions, invisible characters, curl | sh installs, downloaded programs, credential reads, persistence and the authors Snyk's ToxicSkills research confirmed malicious. Plugin hooks are listed with the events that run them.

item.title: Cursor marketplace Claude Code extension backdoor
item.description: Flags any trace of the tampered 2.1.312 / 2.1.313 builds from 29 October: the svc-telemetry SSH key, its persistence files, launch agent and cron entry.

item.title: Ubuntu's -proposed kernels for CVE-2026-98432
item.description: A booted -proposed kernel now counts as fixed, and the fix plan gives Ubuntu's own steps to install it.

item.title: AI agent setup audit
item.description: Unpinned MCP servers, coding agents allowed to run any command, SSH keys without a passphrase and .env files in folders agents work in. Reported as review, never as affected.

item.title: PostgreSQL, psqlODBC and pgAdmin 4
item.description: The August server and client release (fixed in 18.6 / 17.11 / 16.15 / 15.19 / 14.24), the psqlODBC batch fixed in 18.00.0006, and pgAdmin 4, whose fixes aren't released yet.

item.title: python-jose, @fastify/http-proxy, FreeRDP, WordPress plugins, Control Web Panel
item.description: Five fits from the week's critical CVEs, plus npm lockfile support (package-lock, pnpm, yarn, bun).

item.title: Chromium before 156.0.8078.73
item.description: The four critical bugs fixed on 27 October. The latest Playwright and Puppeteer still ship older builds, so the advice is to run them on your installed Chrome with the sandbox on.

item.title: A daily queue of new CVEs
item.description: Every morning a job opens an issue for each newly exploited or newly published CVE the tool doesn't cover yet, so nothing waits for us to notice it.

item.title: macOS Chrome GPU sandbox escape
item.description: CVE-2026-106378, fixed in 155.0.8059.39, flagged on Macs only.

item.title: Exploited Chrome bugs, stale Puppeteer and Playwright browsers, archived MCP servers
item.description: Installed Chrome, the Chromium copies Puppeteer and Playwright cache and never update, and MCP configs still running the archived Puppeteer server. Also SECURITY.md and private vulnerability reporting.

item.title: Linux servers
item.description: On Ubuntu, Debian and RHEL-family servers: the running kernel, nginx, Apache, MariaDB, MongoDB, WordPress and more, judged against each distro's own fixed packages.

item.title: amiaffected.now and the one-liner
item.description: curl -fsSL https://amiaffected.now/run | sh, readable before you run it.

item.title: Stale-data warning
item.description: Each run checks the public cve.now feed and warns when newer CVEs exist for what it tracks. Nothing about your machine is sent.

item.title: First release
item.description: The October 2026 PHP, Node.js, BIND, LiteLLM, GitLab and eMudhra issues, Docker image scanning and a fix plan with the exact commands.
